conclusion: The inert observer theorem is a strict positive branch.  It covers the E x S_3 derived-route boundary example but is too narrow for Type A sequential gauges and Type B flip-across routing.  Those require the existing active-factor/transducer certificate framework.

theorem: If maps o:X->I and q:X->Y to a finite rack Y satisfy o(u)=o(x), o(v)=o(y), and (q(u),q(v))=r_Y(q(x),q(y)) for every r_X(x,y)=(u,v), and x->(o(x),q(x)) is injective, then X^n is B_n-isomorphic to a B_n-invariant subset of Y^n x I^n with I^n fixed pointwise.  If the map is bijective onto Y x I on one letters, then ker rho^X_n = ker rho^Y_n for all n.
